name: Khim Singh Mohan Singh Rautela Sweets
why_it_matters: Started by brothers Kheem Singh and Mohan Singh Rautela near the KMOU bus station after they trained in Joga Lal Sah's halwai shop. The most popular bal mithai counter in Almora — roasted khoya cubes coated with sugar-pearl poppy seeds, the recipe unchanged for over a century. State-sweet status of Uttarakhand.
insider_tip: Cash only — no UPI or card. Open 6:30am-8pm; pick up a kilo at ₹380 before catching a Roadways bus, the shop is steps from the stand.
signature_address: Mall Road, near Roadways Bus Station, Almora 263601

name: Lala Joga Sah
why_it_matters: The actual origin shop of bal mithai — Lala Joga Lal Sah set up here in 1865 and is credited with inventing the khoya-and-sugar-pearl sweet that became Uttarakhand's state mithai. Now run by Harish Lal Shah, the fifth-generation owner. Less famous than Rautela's but the founding lineage.
insider_tip: Ask for the singauri — fresh khoya wrapped in a malu (oak) leaf cone. Eat it the same day; the leaf gives a herbal note that fades by morning.

name: Glory Restaurant
why_it_matters: One of Almora's oldest sit-down restaurants — multi-cuisine menu covering north Indian, Chinese and south Indian, with a dependable kitchen since 1964. Where local families and out-of-town visitors converge for the butter chicken-and-naan default.
insider_tip: The Mughlai side outperforms the Chinese — order butter chicken with tandoori roti rather than the chowmein. Around ₹500 for two; near Hotel Shikhar on the L. R. Sah Road stretch of Mall Road.
signature_address: Shagun Complex, First Floor, L. R. Sah Road, Khatyari, Almora 263601

name: Soni Restaurant
why_it_matters: A no-frills Paltan Bazar fixture since 1972 — owner-run, cramped seating, north Indian veg and non-veg done well at hill-town prices. The kind of place taxi drivers recommend before any guidebook.
insider_tip: Opens 11:30am, often a wait by 1pm. Portions are generous — order one curry and one dal between two and you'll be fine. Walking distance from the nagar palika office.
signature_address: Near Nagar Palika Parishad, Paltan Bazar, Palari Garh, Almora 263601

name: Hotel Shikhar Restaurant
why_it_matters: The dining room at Hotel Shikhar — opened 1989 at Shikhar Tiraha, the central crossroads on Mall Road. One of the few Almora kitchens that runs a serious Kumaoni section alongside continental and north Indian, served on a terrace with valley views.
insider_tip: Ask for the Kumaoni thali specifically — it's not always pushed at non-Indian guests. High tea on the balcony 4-6pm catches the best afternoon light over the ridge.

name: The Cafe Almora
why_it_matters: The Almora youth-and-tourist hangout — Indo-Chinese, momos, burgers, sandwiches, well-priced. Located near the Head Post Office, walkable from Mall Road. Where you go when you want a chicken roll instead of a thali.
insider_tip: The crispy veg kurkure momos are the under-the-radar order — better than the standard steamed version. Skip dessert and walk to a sweet shop on Lala Bazar instead.
signature_address: Near Head Post Office, Dharanaula, Almora 263601

name: The Kasar Kitchen
why_it_matters: On the Kasar Devi-Binsar road next to the KMVN tourist rest house — wood-and-stone tables, Himalayan view, kitchen that does Kumaoni mutton thali alongside the foreign-traveller staples. One of the few hill restaurants serious about local ingredients (farm vegetables, pahadi khoya, hemp-seed bhaang chutney).
insider_tip: Order the Kumaoni thali with mutton (not the mixed Asian items) — that's where the kitchen delivers. Call ahead +91 95363 61171 in season; only 50 covers, and Kasar Devi crowds drop in unpredictably.
signature_address: Deenapani, Kasar Devi-Binsar Road, near KMVN Tourist Rest House, Almora 263601

name: Dolma Restaurant
why_it_matters: Family-run Tibetan kitchen at walking distance from the Kasar Devi temple — thukpa, momos, chowmein, both veg and non-veg. The closest thing Almora has to a Manali-style Tibetan canteen, with a Himalayan view from the parking lot.
insider_tip: Mutton momos and thukpa are the kitchen's strengths; the Indian dishes are filler. Vegetarian options are limited — stick to veg thukpa or veg chowmein. Hygiene is variable in monsoon; go in dry season.
signature_address: Kasar Devi Road, near Kasar Devi Temple, Almora 263601

name: Mohan's Cafe
why_it_matters: The Crank's Ridge institution — owner Mohan built Binsar Retreat from a single mud cottage. Cafe at the top of the property does Indian, continental and Israeli (shakshuka, hummus) for the long-stay traveller crowd that's come to Kasar Devi since the Beats. Wooden furniture, thatch roof, 90s playlist.
insider_tip: Service can be brusque — go for the food and the view, not for warm hospitality. The cafe sits higher than Dolma; the Himalayan panorama at sunset is the actual reason to climb up.
signature_address: Crank's Ridge, Kasar Devi-Binsar-Bageshwar Road, Almora 263601
